text:
Slew is the only failing spec, and it's a moderate miss: 13.5 MV/s simulated against the 15 MV/s target. Slew tracks tail current almost one-for-one (+10% current gives +10% slew), so the fix is more tail current.

Power can absorb it. The simulated currents were 10 + 34 + 168 µA, and the tail is only reaching about 84% of its programmed value. Raising the tail to 60 µA programmed (≈50 µA actual) while trimming the output stage to 125 µA gives about 10 + 50 + 150 µA. That is roughly 420 µW at 1.98 V, under the 530 µW limit.

The extra input current also raises gm and unity-gain bandwidth. Phase margin is at 84°, so there is room for that. A slightly larger Cc keeps the phase margin safe at ff corners.

{"action": "refine", "reason": "Only slew fails (0.9x). Slew scales ~1:1 with itail; raise itail to ~60uA (power headroom exists), trim i7 to keep power <450uW, slightly higher gmid1. PM 84 deg leaves room for higher UGBW. Widen itail upper bound for ss/125C slew margin.", "params": {"itail": 60e-6, "i7": 125e-6, "gmid1": 18.0, "cc": 1.3e-12}, "bounds": {"itail": [45e-6, 80e-6], "i7": [100e-6, 160e-6], "cc": [0.9e-12, 1.8e-12]}}
